voiceEvents.meaning: I am Santiago Cundumi Solis and this is my STEAM project: Water Rocket Competition.
If the gas escapes too early, less pressure remains for launch.
I assembled the setup, tested it in the patio and recorded the attempts.
I learned that I needed to record quantities, height and flight time.
I adjusted the assembly between one test and the next.
It rose, but only reached approximately half a metre.
For the final design, I added fins and a supporting base.
I put the fins at the rear to help the rocket maintain its direction. With airflow, they help correct small tilts.
The green base holds the rocket upright before takeoff. Its role is support during preparation.
The conical nose helps air flow around the rocket with less resistance than a flat front.
I also fastened the pieces with tape to keep the assembly together. With these changes I prepared the final test.
Gas raises the pressure inside the bottle. Expelling liquid downward produces upward thrust and gives the rocket kinetic energy.
Estimate additional rise after thrust from vertical velocity. An assumed 10 m/s gives 5.1 m in the ideal model. This ignores drag and is an example, not a measurement of the flight.

finalFootageEvidence: Upward movement at 382.812 seconds, followed by an unsupported descent. The foreground leg obscures the release mechanism. Height is the student's retrospective estimate, not a calibrated video measurement.
